title: Not Getting Angry
note: This means not getting angry even when you have cause. It forbids the anger that arises from lying, so it follows the chapter on truthfulness.

couplets.plain: Whoever holds back anger where it can take effect truly holds it back. Where it can’t, what does it matter if you hold it back or not?
couplets.pm: Only someone who stops anger from rising, out of compassion, where it would take effect, is truly holding it back. “Where it would” means against those weaker than you in ascetic power, and “where it wouldn’t” against the stronger. With them anger does no harm, so there is no righteousness in holding it back or in letting it go.

links.quote: holds back anger where it can take effect
links.reason: Holding back only means something where your anger could take effect.

links.quote: what does it matter if you hold it back or not
links.reason: Anger held in where it could do damage is the only restraint that counts.

couplets.plain: Anger is bad where it can’t take effect. Where it can, nothing is worse.
couplets.pm: Anger that rises against the stronger is bad for you alone, since all it brings is trouble from them in this life. Anger against the weak brings blame in this life and sin in the next, so nothing is worse. Anger is wrong anywhere.
couplets.sensitive: calls anger wrong even in someone helpless

links.quote: Anger is bad where it can’t take effect
links.reason: Leaves anger no excuse: bad where it can’t take effect, and at its worst where it can.

links.quote: Where it can, nothing is worse
links.reason: Someone whose anger can take effect on others is told that nothing is worse.

couplets.plain: Forget your anger, whoever it is against. Evil things are born of it.
couplets.pm: Give up anger against everyone, whether stronger, equal or weaker, because all evil arises from it. It breeds every bad thought that those who have renounced in their hearts must not have.
couplets.sensitive: tells the wronged to drop anger at any offender

links.quote: Evil things are born of it
links.reason: Allows no exception for anyone, since evil things are born of anger.

links.quote: Forget your anger, whoever it is against

couplets.plain: Anger kills your smile and your joy. What other enemy is there?
couplets.pm: For those who have renounced, compassion brings a smile to the face and joy to the heart. Anger rises by killing both, and there is no other enemy. They have no enemies outside, but this enemy within drives away compassion and their other friends, and brings the suffering of rebirth.

links.reason: Counts what it kills, the smile and the joy, and finds no other enemy to match it.

couplets.plain: If you would guard yourself, guard against anger. If you don’t, it is you that anger kills.
couplets.pm: If you mean to keep yourself from suffering, keep anger out of your mind. If not, it brings you terrible suffering. Ascetics who spend their penance on curses lose what would have given them all they wished, and bear the pain of that penance and of rebirth together. “Kills” here means extreme suffering.

links.quote: it is you that anger kills
links.reason: Turns anger back on its owner: left unguarded, the one it kills is you.

links.quote: If you would guard yourself, guard against anger

couplets.plain: Anger, the killer of those who come near it, burns the raft of safety that is your own people.
couplets.pm: The fire called anger burns not only those it touches but the raft that would save them. Your people here are those who have fully renounced, great in penance and wisdom, whose sweet words do you good. They bring you across the sea of births to the shore of release. Anger sinks you and drives away those who would lift you out.

links.quote: burns the raft of safety that is your own people
links.reason: Says the damage spreads past the angry person to the people who keep them safe.

links.quote: the killer of those who come near it, burns
links.reason: Anger acts as a fire here, killing whoever comes near it and burning your own people too.
Calls your own people a raft of safety, and anger is what burns it.

couplets.plain: Someone who prizes anger will be ruined, as surely as a hand that strikes the ground can’t escape.
couplets.pm: Someone who takes anger for a quality that shows their power will lose that power. This is as certain as a hand struck at the ground reaching the ground.
couplets.note: பிழையாது can mean the hand “won’t escape” being hurt, or “won’t miss”. He takes it as won’t miss: the blow can’t fail to land.

links.quote: a hand that strikes the ground can’t escape
links.reason: Pictures prized anger as a blow struck on the ground, with ruin as certain for the one who strikes.

couplets.plain: Even if someone hurts you as a mass of flame would, it is good not to be angry, if you can.
couplets.pm: Though someone does you harm again and again, like a great blaze of many flames touching you, it is good if you can keep from anger. “If you can” shows that such treatment would anger even sages.
couplets.sensitive: urges no anger even under severe mistreatment

links.quote: it is good not to be angry, if you can
Even if someone hurts you as a mass of flame would
as a mass of flame would

couplets.plain: If you never even think of anger in your heart, all you have thought of will come to you at once.
couplets.pm: An ascetic who never thinks of anger in his heart gets all the rewards he aims at, all together. The heart meant is the compassionate heart, and not thinking of anger means growing compassion until anger is wholly gone. This life, the next and release are different things, yet this one practice brings them all.

links.quote: never even think of anger in your heart

couplets.plain: Those far gone in anger are like the dead. Those who renounce anger are the equals of renouncers.
couplets.pm: Those far gone in anger are alive, yet like the dead: life remains in which to reach wisdom, but their turmoil means they surely won’t. Those who give up anger must still die, yet they equal those who are free of death: the body remains, but their wisdom makes release certain.

links.quote: Those who renounce anger are the equals of renouncers
links.reason: Divides people by it: those far gone in anger are like the dead, and those who renounce it equal the renouncers.

links.quote: Those far gone in anger are like the dead
links.reason: Someone far gone in anger still breathes but is counted among the dead.
